div.div: Fog nodes and device IDs hash onto the same identifier ring (SHA-1, m bits). A device's state belongs to the first node clockwise from its key, so a node joining or leaving only moves the keys next to it.

ul.li: key = SHA-1(device SPIFFE ID); owner = successor(key)
the owner keeps the device's windows and IDS state, so detectors are not split across nodes
membership changes come from SWIM; only neighbouring keys move

text.tspan: How ZTC uses it
key = SHA-1(device SPIFFE ID); owner =
successor(key)GET /v1/owner?device=… on any fog
nodethe owner keeps the device's windows and IDS
state, so detectors are not split across
nodesmembership changes come from SWIM; only
neighbouring keys move

div.b: Design choice: why a DHT at all?

ul.li: a central placement table in the cloud would not survive a WAN partition
consistent hashing gives balanced placement without coordination
alternative: rendezvous hashing — simpler, but O(N) per lookup; Chord shows the routing idea

text.tspan: Design choice: why a DHT at all?
a central placement table in the cloud would not survive a WAN partitionconsistent hashing gives balanced placement
without coordinationalternative: rendezvous hashing — simpler, but O(N) per lookup; Chord shows the routing idea

div.div: Security note: ring position is derived from a hash, so a node cannot pick where it lands without grinding IDs; fog identities come from the CA, and state handover between owners uses the same sealed-state mechanism as migration (RQ3).
